blocks.text: Transition elements can exist in several oxidation states, so they take part in many redox reactions. Whether a redox reaction is feasible is decided by comparing the standard electrode potentials (E) of the half-reactions: E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation), and the reaction is feasible if E cell is positive. In practice, the species with the more positive E value is reduced (gains electrons) and the one with the less positive value is oxidised (loses electrons).
